Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

Experience in professional software development
Knowledge of standard speech and machine learning techniques

Job Overview

WHO WE ARE

Relativity is a leading legal data intelligence company building technology that helps users organize data, discover the truth, and act on it with confidence. Our AI-powered, cloud platform, RelativityOne, transforms massive volumes of complex information into actionable insights for litigation, investigations, regulatory inquiries, data breach responses, and other high-stakes legal work where accuracy and trust are crucial.

The world’s largest law firms, corporations, and government agencies rely on Relativity’s legal AI software to securely surface and manage the most relevant and impactful information in their matters. Beyond our commercial impact, we are committed to expanding access to technology and supporting pro bono legal work.

What We Do

claiR is Relativity's conversational AI experience, built for lawyers at the world's leading law firms. Running inside the Relativity aiR platform, claiR is an agentic surface into Relativity's petabytes of matter intelligence, letting users search, enrich, and generate work product from their data, with answers grounded in the matter's documents and backed by citations. The claiR team builds and ships this experience, from the AI and retrieval systems that reason across a matter to the web interface that lawyers and case teams use to explore their data and collaborate.

Job Description And Requirements

Job Description and Requirements

About The Role

This role offers an opportunity to grow as a full-stack AI engineer on the team building claiR, the conversational AI experience lawyers use to ask questions, search, and draft from their matter data. You will work alongside the engineers and applied scientists who build claiR and gain direct exposure to how agentic features are designed, evaluated, and shipped. You will begin with well-defined features across the stack and grow toward end-to-end ownership of agentic features.

This Advanced AI Engineer role is designed for an early-career to mid-level engineer ready to grow quickly. The role reports to a Lead Engineer on claiR at Relativity and may be based remotely in the United States or in our Chicago office.

What You’ll Do

Build features across the full stack of claiR, including agent tools, prompt and context changes, services and API endpoints, and front-end work in the claiR web app.
Work with applied scientists to extend claiR’s agentic functionality with new capabilities and features.
Write and extend evaluations, run them, and learn to interpret the results. Ship changes behind feature flags and monitor production outcomes.
Learn and practice a modern software development lifecycle from day one through small, frequent commits, feature-flagged deployments, fast rollbacks, and best-in-class agentic engineering tools.
Fix bugs, improve reliability, and add tests while developing an understanding of how agentic systems fail.
Pair with Senior and Lead engineers on design and code reviews. Ask questions and document what you learn so others can benefit.
Take on increasingly ambiguous problems as you demonstrate readiness.

Required

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

2+ years of professional software development experience or equivalent demonstrated ability, such as a strong open-source track record, a shipped product, or substantial internship experience.
Working proficiency in Python and C#, plus hands-on experience building full-stack web applications with a front end such as React, services, and a relational database using SQL.
Hands-on experience building an agentic solution with LLMs, even at a small scale, such as an agent, a retrieval-augmented generation application, or a tool-using assistant. Ability to explain system prompts, tool calls, embeddings, and common failure points.
Basic familiarity with cloud services such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, containers, and CI/CD.
Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and writing clean, tested code.
Clear written and spoken English and a preference for simple solutions over clever ones.

WHY WE COULD BE A GREAT FIT

Impactful Mission

Build systems that help customers organize data, discover the truth, and act on it in high-stakes legal matters.

Engineering at Scale

Work on distributed, cloud-native systems that process large volumes of data.

Cutting-Edge Technology

Build with AI, cloud platforms, and scalable architectures shaping legal tech.

Growth and Ownership

Gain experience owning systems end-to-end across cloud and distributed environments.

Collaborative Culture

Work in a team focused on knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

Inclusive Environment

Diverse perspectives create stronger teams and better outcomes.

Compensation And Benefits

Competitive salary, benefits, DTO, parental leave, and equity program.

Relativity is committed to competitive, fair, and equitable compensation practices.

This position is eligible for total compensation which includes a competitive base salary, an annual performance bonus, and long-term incentives.

$120,000 and $180,000

The final offered salary will be based on several factors, including but not limited to the candidate's depth of experience, skill set, qualifications, and internal pay equity. Hiring at the top end of the range would not be typical, to allow for future meaningful salary growth in this position.

Required Skills

Algorithms, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNS), Big Data, Computer Vision, Data Science, Deep Learning, Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Software Engineering

added.description:
What We Need

Corpay is currently looking to hire an AI Agent Developer within our Corporate Payments division. This position falls under our Account Payables line of business. In this role, the AI Agent Developer is an experienced individual contributor within Corpay Payables’ Data & Analytics organization and AI Center of Excellence (AI CoE), responsible for designing, developing, deploying, and continuously improving enterprise AI Agents that solve real-world business and operational challenges across the Payables division.

This role will help expand Corpay’s AI development capabilities and increase the velocity at which AI Agents move from business idea to production implementation. The AI Agent Developer will build intelligent solutions using large language models (LLMs), agentic AI frameworks, enterprise data, APIs, tools, and workflow automation to support use cases across Payables Operations and other functional areas.

In addition to directly developing AI Agents, this role will help build AI capability across the organization by creating reusable development patterns, standards, training, and hands-on education that enable designated team members within functional areas to independently design, build, test, and implement AI Agents for their respective business needs.

The ideal candidate combines strong software and AI engineering capabilities with practical business judgment. This individual must be comfortable working directly with business stakeholders, translating ambiguous problems into well-defined AI solutions, rapidly prototyping new capabilities, and applying the engineering, security, governance, evaluation, and operational discipline required to move AI solutions into reliable production use.

How We Work

As an AI Agent Developer you will be expected to work in an onsite environment reporting to either our Brentwood, TN or Peachtree Corners, GA office location. Corpay will set you up for success by providing:

Assigned workspace in our Brentwood, TN and Peachtree Corners, GA office location
Company-issued equipment
Formal, hands-on training

Role Responsibilities

The responsibilities of the role will include:

Designing, developing, testing, deploying, maintaining, and improving enterprise AI agents and LLM-powered applications for Payables business and operational needs.
Partnering with business teams to understand processes, identify AI opportunities, gather requirements, and turn needs into technical solutions.
Building AI agent workflows that can retrieve information, use data, call APIs and tools, complete tasks, and securely connect with company systems.
Developing solutions using LLMs and enterprise AI platforms such as OpenAI/ChatGPT, Azure OpenAI, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Fabric, Claude, or similar tools.
Building RAG solutions using company documents, databases, knowledge repositories, vector stores, and approved data sources.
Connecting AI agents with company applications through APIs, databases, SDKs, MCP-compatible services, connectors, and other integration methods.
Creating effective prompts, system instructions, context strategies, tool definitions, structured outputs, and multi-step agent workflows.
Deciding when to use AI, business rules, traditional software, workflow automation, or human review within a process.
Creating reusable AI components, templates, frameworks, connectors, testing methods, and development patterns.
Establishing standards and repeatable practices that help AI solutions scale across Payables.
Creating training materials, examples, documentation, and learning experiences for functional teams.
Coaching and guiding Payables team members as they begin building AI agents for their own areas.
Supporting teams in following architecture, security, evaluation, governance, and development standards while enabling safe self-service AI development.
Reviewing and advising on agents built by functional teams to ensure they meet production-readiness and responsible-AI standards.
Creating automated and human evaluation methods for measuring accuracy, relevance, completeness, task success, response time, cost, and user satisfaction.
Developing test cases, golden datasets, regression tests, and other methods for consistently assessing agent behavior.
Identifying and reducing AI risks such as hallucinations, incorrect tool use, incomplete retrieval, prompt injection, inappropriate actions, and data leakage.
Implementing validation, grounding, guardrails, permissions, authentication, authorization, human review, and escalation processes based on risk.
Protecting confidential company information and following Corpay security, privacy, governance, and responsible-AI standards.
Optimizing AI solutions for performance, token use, response time, cost, reliability, scalability, and user experience.
Testing new AI capabilities through proofs of concept and rapid prototypes to determine business value and production readiness.
Applying engineering best practices when moving successful prototypes into production, including testing, version control, code review, documentation, deployment, monitoring, and support.
Monitoring live AI agents through telemetry, user feedback, evaluation results, operational metrics, and business KPIs.
Investigating AI-agent failures, finding root causes, and implementing fixes to improve reliability.
Documenting AI architectures, prompts, workflows, data sources, integrations, dependencies, tools, evaluations, security considerations, and operating procedures.
Collaborating with Data Engineering, Analytics, Software Engineering, Architecture, Information Security, Operations, and other teams to launch and support AI solutions.
Explaining AI capabilities, limitations, risks, recommendations, and expected business value to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Helping stakeholders identify which opportunities are best suited for AI versus traditional automation, analytics, software, or process improvement.
Contributing to the AI Center of Excellence’s standards, methods, reusable assets, governance practices, and delivery approach.
Staying current on new developments in generative AI, agentic AI, LLMs, multimodal models, evaluation, security, governance, and enterprise AI platforms.
Evaluating new AI tools and approaches based on business value, reliability, security, scalability, maintainability, and production readiness.

Qualifications & Skills

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
3+ years of relevant experience in AI application development, automation, machine learning, data engineering, software development, or a related technical discipline.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building AI, LLM-powered, automation, or intelligent application solutions.
Strong application-development skills using Python and experience working with REST APIs, JSON, SDKs, authentication mechanisms, and enterprise integrations.
Experience working with one or more LLM platforms or APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or comparable technologies.
Understanding of LLM concepts including prompts, system instructions, tokens, context windows, structured outputs, tool/function calling, model selection, reasoning models, and model limitations.
Experience designing or implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation, embeddings, semantic search, document retrieval, vector search, or other enterprise knowledge-grounding solutions.
Understanding of agentic AI concepts, including tool-enabled agents, multi-step workflows, context management, state, memory, validation, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Working knowledge of relational databases and SQL sufficient to enable AI applications to securely consume, investigate, and reason across structured enterprise data.
Strong understanding of software engineering practices including modular design, debugging, testing, version control, Git, code review, deployment, and production support.

This position is part of the Enterprise Data Services Division--we own the company's metric definitions, the semantic layer that serves them, and an AI-powered analytics platform built on top. Metric logic lives in version-controlled code; agents and applications read from it rather than reinventing it.

This is an engineering role, not a prompt-writing role. Most of the platform's skills are deterministic Python, with AI agents orchestrating them. You'll spend more time making things correct, tested, and reliable than making them clever.

Agents And Skills Management

Build, test, and maintain the Python skills and AI agents that run on the platform.
Keep a clean skills catalog: versioning, documentation, ownership, and retiring skills that are no longer used.
Build evaluation and regression checks (test sets, validators, output-format rules) so agent quality is consistent from run to run.
Monitor agent usage, cost, and failures, and fix the root cause rather than the symptom.

Platform backend maintenance

Maintain the platform's agent runtime, built on a TypeScript agent framework (Mastra): agent workflows, tool definitions, memory, and model configuration.
Maintain MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and connectors that link agents to the warehouse, semantic layer, BI tools, and other company systems.
Keep the platform's API services, scheduled jobs, and data pipelines healthy; handle framework, SDK, and model version upgrades.
Triage and resolve failed jobs, broken connectors, data-quality alerts, and user-reported issues.
Improve CI/CD, logging, and monitoring so problems surface before users find them.
Write runbooks so any teammate can operate the platform.

Data foundation (working knowledge)

Understand how the gold data layer and semantic models feed the platform, and make small, reviewed changes to them.
Work with the metric tree, the map of how business metrics drive each other, to connect new metrics and their relationships to the platform.
Trace a number from the platform back to its source data when something looks wrong.

Qualifications

Minimum

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant quantitative, technical, engineering, or business-related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred

Masters Degree in a quantitative field
CS, engineering, math, or stats degree preferred

Typically requires 2 years of relevant experience in AI native analytics

Experience with native AI implementations in Insurance industry

Programming

Python: writes, tests, and debugs modular code independently. Deterministic Python
TypeScript/JavaScript: can read and change an existing backend codebase. Mastra is TS-based, so this is required.
SQL: joins, aggregations, and window functions against a warehouse; can sanity-check a metric's output.

Has built at least one working LLM application end to end, such as a tool-calling agent, a RAG app, or an MCP server. A shipped side project counts.
Understands prompts versus tools versus retrieval, context limits, and why agent output is nondeterministic.
Has an instinct for evaluation: tests agent output against expected answers instead of eyeballing it.

Engineering hygiene

Daily use of Git and GitHub: branches, PRs, code review
Works with REST or JSON APIs and reads API documentation without direct supervision

Data and domain basics (concepts only)

Understands what a semantic layer, dimension, and metric are, and how they differ from raw tables
Can read a dbt model and YAML config and follow the lineage

Collaborative. Respectful. A place to dream and do. These are just a few words that describe what life is like at Toyota. Toyota Financial Services Enterprise Platforms team is looking for a passionate and highly motivated AI/ML Platform Engineer
. This role helps build and operate cloud-native platform capabilities that enable enterprise MLOps and LLMOps and support AI/ML and GenAI application delivery. You will contribute hands-on engineering across APIs, services, deployment pipelines, and platform automation, working closely with senior engineers, architecture, platform, data, and product teams.

Design, build, test, and maintain cloud-native platform components and services that support AI/ML and LLM workloads.
Help implement and operate MLOps and LLMOps capabilities such as model deployment pipelines, monitoring, and operational reliability.

2 or more years of professional software engineering experience.

Strong programming skills in one or more of the following: Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript.

Eagerness to learn AI/ML platform engineering and grow under mentorship.

Hands-on exposure to AI/ML platform tools and patterns (MLOps/LLMOps fundamentals).

added.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Diligent is the AI leader in governance, risk and compliance (GRC) SaaS solutions, helping more than 1 million users and 700,000 board members to clarify risk and elevate governance. The Diligent One Platform gives practitioners, the C-Suite and the board a consolidated view of their entire GRC practice so they can more effectively manage risk, build greater resilience and make better decisions, faster.

At Diligent, we're building the future with people who think boldly and move fast. Whether you're designing systems that leverage large language models or part of a team reimaging workflows with AI, you'll help us unlock entirely new ways of working and thinking. Curiosity is in our DNA, we look for individuals willing to ask the big questions and experiment fearlessly - those who embrace change not as a challenge, but as an opportunity. The future belongs to those who keep learning, and we are building it together. At Diligent, you’re not just building the future - you’re an agent of positive change, joining a global community on a mission to make an impact.

A Day in the Life

You’ll build AI agents that carry out complex, multi-step workflows for governance, risk, compliance and internal audit professionals. Working directly with enterprise customers, you’ll turn an understanding of their processes into software they can depend on in production.

You’ll deliver on a shared agent platform, combining infrastructure, connectors, services and user-facing components into solutions for different workflows. With Platform Engineering and fellow FDEs, you’ll turn patterns from customer delivery into building blocks others can use.

What you’ll do

Embed with major enterprise customers across the EU and US. Work with internal audit, risk, compliance and governance teams to understand their processes, decision points, data sources and operational constraints.
Participate in agent-focused discovery workshops. Map workflows with practitioners, identify where automation will help, and choose an agent or simpler software according to the problem. Agree what a useful result looks like before building.
Build prototypes quickly and test them with practitioners. Use feedback to refine scope, expose assumptions and establish what needs to change before production.
Assemble solutions from existing platform capabilities and extend them where needed. Build backend services, data pipelines, API integrations and agent tools using appropriate languages, frameworks and cloud services. Python, TypeScript and AWS are likely parts of the toolkit; choices will depend on the solution and platform requirements.
Take agents through production deployment and continued evaluation. Build golden datasets, evaluation infrastructure, guardrails and observability to assess outputs, investigate failures and detect regressions.
Make delivery trade-offs explicit with customers and engineering colleagues. Explain reliability limits, human review needs and remaining risks. Keep practitioners and senior stakeholders informed.
Contribute reusable capabilities with Platform Engineering and other FDEs. Separate common workflow logic from customer-specific details, and develop shared components, connectors and enhancements with clear interfaces, tests and documentation. Bring evidence across accounts to product and engineering discussions about platform improvements.
Use coding agents throughout development to explore implementations, write code and tests, and investigate failures. Review generated changes for correctness, security and maintainability, and verify behavior before production. You remain accountable for the software you ship.

What you’ll bring

Hands-on experience shipping at least one SaaS production agent through prototyping, evaluation, live deployment and regression testing. Explain what you built, how you established quality and what changed after deployment.
A deep understanding of the agent development life cycle, including evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, prompt versioning and golden datasets, and how these practices keep deployed agents dependable.
Strong software engineering fundamentals and production coding ability in relevant languages. Your experience includes APIs, data pipelines, backend services and agent tool-calling frameworks such as MCP or an equivalent. You can learn and select technologies to fit the problem. Python, TypeScript and AWS are useful examples, rather than a fixed stack requirement.
Experience developing software with coding agents and harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or comparable tools. You can scope their work, supply context, critically review generated code and validate changes through testing and debugging.
The ability to recognize reusable patterns in customer work and develop them with other engineers into shared capabilities. You can explain where an abstraction helps, where customer-specific logic belongs and how to evolve shared components safely.
Experience with multi-agent orchestration, including orchestrator/sub-agent architectures, agent-to-agent coordination and shared context models. You understand how responsibilities and context move between agents and how to investigate coordination failures.
The ability to work effectively with senior enterprise stakeholders, including company boards and executive leadership teams (ELTs), and to debug a failing agent trace. You explain technical choices and limitations clearly.
Curiosity about governance, risk, compliance and audit, with the drive to learn unfamiliar processes through direct work with practitioners. A compliance background is not required.
Flexibility to travel regularly across EU and US customer sites.

Helpful experience

Familiarity with GRC, audit or compliance software platforms and their workflows.
Previous forward-deployed, solutions engineering or embedded customer-facing engineering work. An FDE title is not required to demonstrate the capabilities above.
Exposure to LLMOps tooling for tracing, prompt versioning, evaluation at scale and regression testing frameworks, complementing the life-cycle understanding required above.

What Diligent Offers You

Pay Range

Incentive Compensation

Offers will be negotiated based on each candidate's qualifications.

This role is eligible to participate in our annual incentive plan. Incentives are earned based on employee performance against defined metrics and company goals.

Benefits

Full-time roles are eligible for our comprehensive benefits program which includes medical, dental and vision coverage. You may also contribute to our 401(k) plan that includes a company match.

Creativity is ingrained in our culture. We are innovative collaborators by nature. We thrive in exploring how things can be differently both in our internal processes and to help our clients. We care about our people. Diligent offers a flexible work environment, global days of service, comprehensive health benefits, meeting free days, generous time off policy and wellness programs. (among others) Diversity is important to us. Growing, maintaining and promoting a diverse team is a top priority for us. We foster and encourage diversity through our Employee Resource Groups and provide access to resources and education to support the education of our team, facilitate dialogue, and foster understanding.

Diligent created the modern governance movement. Our world-changing idea is to empower leaders with the technology, insights and connections they need to drive greater impact and accountability – to lead with purpose. Our employees are passionate, smart, and creative people who not only want to help build the software company of the future, but who want to make the world a more sustainable, equitable and better place.

Headquartered in New York, Diligent has offices in Washington D.C., London, Galway, Budapest, Vancouver, Bengaluru, Munich, Singapore and Sydney.  To foster strong collaboration and connection, this role will follow a hybrid work model. If you are within a commuting distance to one of our Diligent office locations, you will be expected to work onsite at least 50% of the time. We believe that in-person engagement helps drive innovation, teamwork, and a strong sense of community.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
About the company

Our client is an early-stage company building decision intelligence for industrial operations. Its platform builds a live model of a customer's operation, capturing both the data and the reasoning behind each decision, and then deploys AI agents for the revenue, operational, and capital decisions that manufacturers, materials companies, and logistics operators face every day. The team is about a dozen people, led by repeat founders with multiple successful exits.

The role

Every deployment pairs engineers with the customer's experts until a production workflow runs on their data. You will lead the deployment for one customer at a time inside a delivery pod, as the customer's go-to technical lead: you capture how the operation works, then build the data model and agents that run it.

What you'll do

• Lead workflow capture on live deployments: expert interviews, process maps, and the data behind each decision
• Build and ship production agents with the customer's experts, tuned to their tolerance for error
• Write tested, documented code the next engineer can pick up
• Build evaluations that show whether an agent's output is right, and fix it when it is not
• Turn customer feedback around quickly during a deployment
• Bring field signal back to product, and make recurring deployment work reusable
• Own the technical relationship with the customer's experts, IT, and executives

What we're looking for

• 2 to 6 years of experience as a forward deployed engineer, software engineer, solutions engineer, or technical consultant (3 to 4 years is the sweet spot)
• Strong hands-on engineering skills and experience shipping production software

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Connected Warfare division’s Mission Command team builds, deploys, integrates, extends, and scales Anduril's software and hardware to deliver mission-critical capabilities to our customers. As the software engineers closest to Anduril customers and end-users, Mission Software Engineers solve technical challenges of operational scenarios while owning the end-to-end delivery of winning capabilities such as Lattice Mesh, Joint All Domain Command & Control, and Anduril's Menace Family-of-Systems.

As a Software Engineer on the Mission Command team, you will build the foundation for a first-of-its-kind platform designed for the tactical edge, solving novel problems across networking, autonomy, systems integration, robotics, and next-generation distributed data layers. Powering resilient, machine-speed decision-making for warfighters and allies—even in contested, disconnected environments—your work will ensure Anduril’s products seamlessly work together and with third parties to deliver customer value. Driven by a “Whatever It Takes” mindset, the Mission Command team balances intentional, long-term system design with the pragmatic tradeoffs needed to meet immediate customer needs. By keeping the mission top-of-mind, you will make sound, scalable engineering decisions to deliver high-quality, expedient software that preemptively addresses the national security challenges of the future.

What You’ll Do

Own software solutions spanning core mesh platforms, data interfaces, and release management deployed directly to customers to scale critical mission capabilities.
Deliver well-architected systems using modern software engineering practices—including code and design reviews—while championing scalability, reliability, testability, portability, and maintainability.
Drive software solutions end-to-end, partnering closely with end-users to translate complex needs into features while balancing user experience with engineering constraints.
Collaborate across multiple teams to plan, build, and test complex, cross-functional functionality.
Ensure system health and rapid resolution by creating and analyzing monitoring metrics, triaging production issues, root-causing failures, and coordinating next steps.
Be embedded onsite at customer locations at least 50% of the timen (primarily military sites), working alongside end-users to navigate real-world operating environments and build, test, and deploy mission-critical capabilities directly in the field.

Required Qualifications

Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret Clearance
Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Networking, Mathematics, or Physics
At least 3-10+ years working with a variety of programming languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, etc.
Experience building software solutions involving significant amounts of data processing and analysis
Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and established code bases

About The Role

Fora is moving AI beyond isolated initiatives and into the systems and workflows powering our Growth, Marketing and Sales teams.

As Forward Deployed AI Solutions (GTM), you'll work directly alongside our teams to identify high-impact opportunities, redesign workflows and build AI-powered agents, tools and automations that drive growth and operational efficiency.

You'll move rapidly from idea to production, integrating and extending our existing platforms, then scaling what works across teams. You'll also empower teams to adopt, operate and build on the solutions you ship.

: Fluent in LLM APIs, agent frameworks, tool calling, integrations and workflow automation, with the ability to build and iterate independently.
Production-minded execution
: Experience taking solutions from prototype to production, with sound judgment on reliability, security and when to involve Engineering.
Commercial problem-solving
: Able to translate business challenges into practical AI solutions, prioritizing measurable outcomes over technical complexity.
Forward-deployed mindset:
Comfortable working directly with business teams, understanding their workflows, moving quickly and driving adoption beyond launch.

Strongly Preferred

Experience with CRM/CDP platforms, including AI-powered automation and decisioning.
Experience applying AI to paid media, CRO, campaign optimization or experimentation.
Experience with BigQuery, Segment or similar data platforms, connecting warehouse data to AI agents and operational workflows.

Unlimited vacation

Dental & Vision Insurance
Wellhub Memberships

Commuter Benefits

Stock Options

We’re forging our own path

Fora has always been about driving change within the industry. We’re not interested in maintaining the status quo.

We’re stronger together

Community is our cornerstone and collective power is our strength. We believe we can all go further when we operate together, using our combined leverage to unlock better opportunities and outcomes for our advisors, partners, and travelers.

We believe technology is an answer to some of the most fundamental challenges the travel industry faces. added.description:
Solutions Architect, Healthcare AI
Full-Time
Hybrid - DC Area

Solutions architect who can sit in a design session with clinicians, operations staff, and IT leads at a federal health agency, understand what’s actually broken, and put a working prototype in front of them before the next meeting. You’re the person who looks at a clunky, long-standing process and sees three better ways to run it, then tests the best one with the people who do the work instead of debating it on a whiteboard. The role reports directly to the Director, Growth & Deployment Strategy. If you’re good at decomposing interconnected systems to find where the work really breaks down, and you build with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, or a similar tool every day, this role was built for you.

JOB SUMMARY
As Solutions Architect, you are the technical lead embedded with our federal health client, working hands-on in a leading commercial healthcare automation platform. You turn design decisions into working solutions: AI-enabled workflows configured on the platform, prototypes users can click through, and integration requirements our integration partners build against. You bring enough business-architecture discipline to understand why a workflow works the way it does before you automate it, and enough technical depth to make the automation real. You work day to day with the Business Analyst and our integration partners, and you’re the person who decides whether a design can actually be built.

Key Responsibilities
· Embed with the agency’s clinical, operational, and IT teams: sit in design sessions, learn the workflow and its constraints, and propose a technical approach on the spot.
· Turn validated future-state designs into working prototypes, sandbox configurations, and AI-enabled workflows.
· Shape how LLM-based agents and AI-enabled workflow logic are used in each workflow, with enough familiarity with prompt and context engineering, tool use, orchestration, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to guide the build and judge whether it fits clinical reality.
· Work with integration partners to connect the automation platform to the agency’s source systems: define the APIs, data mappings, and transformations (JSON, and HL7/FHIR where it applies) they build against, and confirm the result works as designed.
· Map the current-state system landscape well enough to design against it: interfaces, data flows, where the data really lives, and which constraints are technical versus policy.
· Tie every automation to a baseline measurement. “Instrument first, then automate” is the operating rule on this team.
· Demo working functionality to clinical users and program leadership, collect feedback, and iterate in real time.
· Keep a reusable playbook of patterns, configurations, and components so each workflow deploys faster than the last.

Required Qualifications
· 5+ years in solutions engineering, solutions architecture, technical consulting, or IT consulting, including at least two years in a client-facing role where you took a design from whiteboard to working solution.
· Strong technical fluency with APIs, JSON, data mapping, and SQL: enough to specify an integration precisely and work side by side with the integration partners who build it.
· Working familiarity with LLMs and AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar), including prompt and context engineering and agentic workflows, enough to design with them and evaluate what gets built.
· Daily, practical use of AI tools such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or GitHub Copilot to prototype, analyze, and build. You can show us how they changed the way you work.
· Experience working in a cloud environment (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
· Enough business-process and architecture fluency to map a workflow, question a requirement, and explain a trade-off to a clinician or an executive without jargon.
· Ability to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust background investigation; U.S. citizenship required.

Preferred Qualifications
· Healthcare or health-IT experience, such as EHR integration or modernizing clinical and operational workflows; familiarity with HL7 v2 and FHIR.
· Federal or federal-health delivery experience, including building inside agency security and ATO constraints.
· Experience with low-code or workflow-automation platforms as a builder.
· Familiarity with HIPAA and PHI handling in AI systems.
· Working knowledge of Python or another scripting language for quick analysis and prototyping, whether you write it yourself or direct an AI coding tool to write it.
· Exposure to a modern data stack (Databricks, Snowflake, dbt, Power BI, or equivalent).
Compensation & Benefits
· Competitive base salary with incentive compensation tied to program delivery and company performance
· Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off (PTO)
· Hybrid work environment with flexibility for remote work and in-person collaboration days in McLean, VA

The AI Engineer role designs, builds, and operates agentic AI and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) services that automate multi-step business workflows safely and reliably. The position partners with engineering and business stakeholders to deliver deployable, observable AI systems with measurable quality, strong guardrails, and ongoing iteration as tools and best practices evolve.

Education And Experience Required

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered.
5–10 years of software engineering, including 1 to 2 years of building production grade Generative AI solutions (agentic applications and/or RAG).
Hands-on experience taking both agentic applications (multi-step, tool-calling) and RAG systems (retrieval → generation) to production, with deep expertise in at least one and solid working knowledge of the other.
Built and shipped production services and APIs on AWS, with attention to reliability, latency, and cost.
Comfortable with full-stack delivery using Angular and Node/TypeScript to expose AI capabilities to users.
Familiar with CI/CD and standard operational practices (automated builds/releases, monitoring, alerting).

Technical Skills Required

Advanced Python for backend/AI service development, plus Angular/Node (TypeScript) for full-stack delivery.
Practical experience with at least one agent framework (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI) and safe tool calling design (clear tool boundaries, permissions, validation).
Solid understanding of RAG: chunking, embeddings, retrieval, and basic reranking, with at least one vector store (e.g., OpenSearch, Pinecone, pgvector).
Ability to evaluate and improve AI systems using practical quality signals, agent task success and to catch regressions.
Working knowledge of AWS deployment (serverless and/or containers) with logging, monitoring, and alerting.
Familiarity with responsible/secure AI basics: least privilege, data access controls, and guardrails.
Git-based source control and CI/CD, with reliable release and rollback practices.
Clear communication and a collaborative, delivery-oriented mindset.

Responsibilities

Design and build agentic AI applications that carry out multi-step tasks, with explicit tool boundaries, permissions, and safety controls for predictable behavior.
Build and maintain RAG solutions end-to-end (ingestion, embeddings, retrieval, generation), tuned for relevance, latency, and reliability.
Define practical quality metrics for agents (task success, tool-call correctness) and retrieval (relevance, coverage) and iterate on the results.
Integrate tools and data sources via MCP or similar standard interfaces for secure, reusable access.
Deliver Angular/Node interfaces and APIs that make agentic and RAG capabilities usable by business teams.
Deploy and operate AI services on AWS (e.g., Lambda, ECS/EKS) with sound logging, monitoring, and error handling (retries, fallbacks, guardrails).
Enable workflow automation and integration by identifying high-value repetitive processes and delivering AI-driven automation layers that integrate into enterprise systems and platforms.
Create and maintain technical documentation for architectures, interfaces, evaluation approaches, and operational runbooks to support maintainability and auditability.
Collaborate cross-functionally with product/business stakeholders to translate workflows into well-scoped deliverables and to validate outcomes against measurable success criteria.
Other duties as assigned.

Other Duties As Assigned

Provide advisory support to stakeholders on opportunities to improve operational efficiency using agentic workflows and RAG-enabled automation.
Research and recommend emerging AI tooling, evaluation methods, and responsible AI practices that reduce technical debt and improve system quality over time.

About APA

The American Psychological Association (APA) represents 146,000 psychologists, students, and affiliates, primarily in the U.S. and Canada but also in other countries around the world. APA is a scientific and professional organization with about 500 employees and is categorized as a 501(c)(3) along with its 501(c)(6) companion organization, APA Services, Inc.

added.description:
About The Role

Gallatin AI builds AI-driven logistics planning and decision support for military operations. Our AI team is growing quickly, and we are hiring a Principal AI Engineer to be a technical anchor for it: someone who sets the engineering bar, owns architecture and scalability, and helps the team design, build, review, and ship its own work with high quality, in close partnership with our platform and backend teams.

We are looking for an exceptional engineer with broad range and sound judgment. You have designed systems that other engineers build on, you make the people around you better, and you care as much about how a team builds as what it builds. Deep AI experience is a plus. Deep engineering judgment is the requirement.

What You Will Do

Serve as a quality gate for our AI services: hold the bar on design, testing, and scalability, and review the changes that matter most before they ship.
Be accountable for how our AI services integrate with our event-driven backend (NATS-based messaging), data models, and APIs, working with platform and backend engineers to keep those integrations safe, scalable, and consistent.
Be a trusted code reviewer for the AI team, including changes into shared backend and data systems
Build a review culture that scales: clear architecture guidelines, common patterns to follow and avoid, design review templates, and risk-based review tiers, including AI-assisted review, so that quality holds as PR volume grows.
Prevent architectural drift. Make sure engineers working in parallel, with or without AI coding assistants, are building toward the same design instead of undoing each other’s work.
Own scalability: set latency, throughput, concurrency, and cost targets, find bottlenecks, and fix them. Ask “what happens at 10x?” before things ship.
Write production code on difficult problems, including AI-specific backend features, agent and retrieval services, and data pipelines.
Lead design reviews and RFCs and drive them to decisions. Know when infrastructure or data model changes are safe and how to roll them out without breaking existing systems.
Make build-versus-buy and model-selection calls, including self-hosted versus cloud tradeoffs under data-handling and deployment constraints.
Unblock the AI team’s access to data sources, infrastructure, and tooling so they can move on their own.
Mentor engineers, grow future technical leads, and help set the hiring bar.

What You Bring

10+ years of software engineering, with a record of designing and scaling complex production systems through multiple orders of magnitude of growth.
Principal-level backend and distributed systems depth: service design, event-driven and message-based architectures, APIs, data modeling, concurrency, caching, and failure handling.
Demonstrated trust as a code and architecture gatekeeper for a team or platform, and a track record of spreading that capability across other engineers.
Strong computer science fundamentals, applied with judgment.
Deep Python fluency, plus strong TypeScript or comparable full-stack experience.
Production experience with, or the demonstrated ability to quickly ramp on, LLM systems such as RAG, agents, tool use, and evaluation.
Strong testing and observability instincts, including reliable tests around nondeterministic components.
Working fluency with cloud infrastructure, containers, and CI/CD. You can ship what you build.
Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, product leaders, and customers.
Eligibility for a US security clearance.

Bonus Points

Prior principal or staff-level experience on a platform other teams build on.
Experience scaling an engineering organization’s practices, such as review, design standards, and onboarding, as headcount tripled.
Experience with data platforms, feature stores, or ML pipelines.
Experience with optimization, simulation, or logistics systems.
Experience in constrained, air-gapped, or regulated deployments.
Background in military logistics, planning doctrine, or defense programs.

Job Description:

At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. We are tackling the world's toughest health challenges, building a world where complex diseases are prevented and cured, treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Across Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine - Oncology, Immunology, Neuroscience and Cardiopulmonary - and Johnson & Johnson MedTech - Cardiovascular, Orthopaedics, Surgery and Vision - our people work every day to change health for humanity. Johnson & Johnson is ranked #1 in healthcare across S&P 500 companies in the AIDE Institute's AI adoption index, which assesses how AI is applied in practice across workforce, operations and business outcomes, including our work in surgical robotics, digital surgery analytics and imaging systems. At Johnson & Johnson, AI accelerates innovation, improves how we operate, and delivers better outcomes for patients.

The Principal AI Engineer, GenAI Developer Experience is the senior hands-on engineer who designs and builds the developer-facing surface of our Enterprise GenAI Platform, making it straightforward to adopt for an engineer in Oncology clinical development, a MedTech manufacturing product team, or a Supply Chain engineering team. You will own the technical design and implementation of that surface end to end: the Agent Framework SDKs and client libraries, the MCP Gateway API contracts and versioning policy, the Agent/Skills/MCP catalog that makes capabilities discoverable and reusable, the API Marketplace, self-service onboarding automation, reference architectures and templates, and the docs-as-code that hold it all together. Your work consumes the agentic runtimes built by our cloud-aligned agentic engineering teams on Microsoft Azure and AWS. You do not build the runtime; you design the abstractions that make it usable, discoverable, documented and adoptable by engineering teams across multiple sectors like Innovative Medicine, MedTech and our enterprise functions, within the expectations of a regulated healthcare enterprise.

Success in this role is measured in developer outcomes: how quickly a team moves from idea to a validated agent in production, how often teams reuse a catalogued skill instead of rebuilding it, how seldom they need to raise a support request, and how satisfied they are with the platform. As the technical authority for developer experience, you set the engineering standards for SDK, API and template design, mentor platform and developer-tooling engineers, and work alongside the Manager, GenAI Developer Experience to shape the roadmap - grounded in Our Credo, creating an inclusive environment where each person is considered as an individual, respecting diversity and dignity, recognizing merit, and holding yourself to actions that are just and ethical.

Key Responsibilities:

Set the technical direction and architecture for the developer-facing surface of the Enterprise GenAI Platform, and shape its roadmap with the Manager, GenAI Developer Experience — making the engineering trade-offs between new capability, hardening and documentation debt explicit across Innovative Medicine, MedTech and enterprise demands.
Design and own the MCP Gateway's published API contract — OpenAPI specifications, semantic versioning and deprecation policy, backward-compatibility guarantees and contract testing — and engineer the SDK release trains and changelogs consumers depend on.
Design, build and maintain the Agent Framework SDKs and client libraries in Python and TypeScript so a Johnson & Johnson engineer can register a tool, call the Gateway and stand up an agent against the shared runtime through a small, documented surface.
Architect and build the Agent, Skills and MCP catalog and the API Marketplace as the enterprise discovery, reuse and entitlement layer — metadata taxonomy, ownership and lifecycle states, certification tiers, search, reuse tracking, consumer registration, self-service quotas and sandbox versus validated environments.
Engineer the self-service onboarding path from access request to first working agent without manual platform intervention — provisioning, credentials, scaffolding and quickstarts to a documented time target — and build AI capability into the automated deployment pipelines with the Cloud and ISRM teams.
Author reference architectures, starter templates and golden paths for the patterns teams actually build — retrieval-grounded assistants, tool-using agents, content generation workflows and MCP servers — favoring harness engineering and durable workflow over bespoke agent development, and set the engineering standards for open-source platform development.
Consume rather than rebuild: design consistent SDK and Gateway abstractions over the Azure and AWS agentic runtimes and feed developer pain points into their roadmaps with reproducible evidence; surface model engineering’s selection guidance, evaluation results and RAG and Knowledge Graph grounding options as documented choices; and align standards with the software engineering developer experience team.
Make the compliant path the easy path, with AI security and governance and Quality as control owners — engineer guardrail configuration, audit traceability, responsible AI disclosures and ISRM controls into SDK defaults and templates, generate GxP-aware documentation and traceable release records from the pipeline, and integrate emerging compliance frameworks.
Instrument and act on the developer experience measurement system — time to first agent, onboarding completion, catalog reuse, support volume and deflection, SDK adoption and satisfaction surveys — keep docs-as-code tested against shipped behavior, and lead technical enablement through office hours, a community of practice, workshops and migration guides.
Provide technical leadership without direct authority: mentor platform, developer-tooling and API engineers; lead SDK and API contract reviews; represent the consuming engineer in architecture and design reviews; and stay hands-on in the hardest SDK, template and critical-fix work.

Qualifications:

Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in software engineering, platform engineering, developer tooling or API product engineering, including technical lead or architect responsibility for a platform consumed by other engineering teams, is required.
A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or a related technical discipline is required; a Master's degree is preferred.
Demonstrated technical ownership of a developer-facing product or internal developer platform consumed by other engineering teams, as the architect of its API contract, versioning and documentation.
Proven experience designing and shipping SDKs, client libraries or public API surfaces, including deprecation and migration management across multiple consumer teams.
Experience mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar through design reviews, code reviews and standards, influencing across teams without direct authority in an inclusive environment consistent with Our Credo.
Deep working knowledge of Generative AI and agentic engineering concepts - agent frameworks, tool and function calling, Model Context Protocol, retrieval-augmented generation - with hands-on experience building agents, tools or MCP servers.
Experience defining and using adoption and developer-productivity measures to drive technical and roadmap decisions rather than relying on narratives.
Ability to partner effectively across engineering, security, risk and compliance functions and to translate control requirements into defaults and templates that developers will genuinely use.
Experience delivering technology in a regulated environment with formal change control, documentation and audit expectations.
Strong written communication in English, including the ability to author and edit technical documentation that engineers can follow without additional support.
Experience working with cloud platforms - Microsoft Azure and/or AWS - and with CI/CD-driven release practices.

Required Skills:

API design and lifecycle management: REST and event-driven contracts, OpenAPI specifications, semantic versioning, backward compatibility, contract testing and deprecation policy.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) concepts and the ability to expose an MCP Gateway as a documented, entitlement-controlled product surface.
Agent framework and SDK abstraction design - tool registration, function calling, session and context handling - built on top of an existing agentic runtime.

Self-service onboarding and provisioning automation using infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD pipelines.

Developer experience measurement - defining instrumentation, funnels, adoption tracking and satisfaction surveys - and converting findings into prioritized engineering work.

added.title: Applied Scientist, Selling Partner Support Engagement
added.description:
Description

Amazon's Selling Partner Support handles tens of millions of contacts annually worldwide. Our science team is transforming this experience by building AI agents that autonomously resolve seller issues, learn from every interaction, and continuously improve with minimal human intervention. These agents reason and adapt — from understanding the seller's context and selecting the right solution, to routing contacts optimally and automating resolution end-to-end. We do this in deep partnership with multiple engineering and product teams.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist who is excited to work on reinforcement learning, agentic architectures, and large-scale production systems. You will be directly connected to the problems sellers face every day, translating real customer pain into science solutions that operate at massive scale. You will frame ambiguous business challenges as tractable machine learning problems and ship systems that measurably improve millions of seller interactions.

Key job responsibilities

Build evaluation frameworks that measure agent quality across dimensions such as helpfulness, correctness, and safety.
Own research and development of reinforcement-learning based agent improvement systems, from problem formulation through production deployment and impact measurement.
Design approaches to preference learning, reward modeling, and policy optimization for conversational agents operating over real-world tools and APIs.
Collaborate with engineering and product teams to deploy models into production systems serving sellers worldwide.
Contribute to the team's scientific impact through peer review, mentorship, and publications at peer-reviewed venues.

A day in the life

You read the latest research papers and implement new techniques by building rapid prototypes using AI-assisted coding tools, then take what works from prototype to production. You collaborate closely with product managers and engineering teams to translate seller pain points into deployed science solutions. You work with senior scientists to propose experiments and make the case for what to build next. You also stay connected to the seller experience by understanding the real problems sellers face so your models solve what actually matters.

About The Team

Our team is a growing group of scientists building the AI that powers Amazon's seller support experience. We operate across capabilities such as agentic systems, knowledge retrieval, and content automation, each owning distinct problem spaces but sharing evaluation infrastructure and research insights. We work backwards from business problems, deeply understanding the domain and defining success metrics and guardrails. This lets us run parallel experiments, compare approaches rigorously, and ship the best models to production. We publish at both internal and external venues and actively invest in research that compounds over multiple product cycles.

The team sits in Seattle/Vancouver and operates with high autonomy. Scientists own their domains end-to-end, from problem framing through production deployment. We value speed over perfection and experimentation over debate. We value inclusive experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply. The team supports an inclusive learning culture where individual growth is a priority — you will find mentorship, knowledge-sharing, and career-advancing resources here.

Basic Qualifications

Master's degree in computer science, mathematics, statistics, machine learning or equivalent quantitative field
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience with SQL and an RDBMS (e.g., Oracle) or Data Warehouse

Preferred Qualifications

Experience implementing algorithms using both toolkits and self-developed code
Have publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
PhD in Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning, Operations Research, Statistics, or related fields
Demonstrated experience leveraging generative AI tools to enhance workflow efficiency and productivity, with the ability to craft effective prompts and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs in a professional setting
Experience identifying opportunities to integrate AI solutions into products and services to drive business value.
Building and Scaling Agentic System Components like Memory, Retrieval, Reasoning and Tool Calling

added.description:
About ECI

ECI
is the leading global provider of managed services, cybersecurity, and business transformation for mid-market financial services organizations across the globe. From its unmatched range of services, ECI provides stability, security and improved business performance, freeing clients from technology concerns and enabling them to focus on running their businesses. More than 1,000 customers worldwide with over $3 trillion of assets under management put their trust in ECI.

At ECI, we believe success is driven by passion and purpose. Our passion for technology is only surpassed by our commitment to empowering our employees around the world
.

Senior AI Forward Deployed Engineer

Position Summary

ECI is seeking a Senior AI Forward Deployed Engineer to help investment firms, including hedge funds, private equity firms, investment banks, and family offices, put AI to work in their businesses. This hands-on, client-facing engineering role identifies high-value opportunities across deal flow, research, trading, portfolio management, risk, valuations, and middle- and back-office operations, then builds, deploys, and drives adoption of production solutions.

The Senior AI Forward Deployed Engineer operates at the Senior FDE level, requiring 5 or more years of professional software engineering experience. The role independently leads client engagements from discovery and scoping through production deployment, adoption, documentation, and handover, and mentors Associate FDEs and FDEs.

This role will be hybrid
in New York, with regular work at client sites in the New York area and occasional travel.

ECI Description

ECI is a Modern Intelligent Service Provider serving alternative investment and banking firms across the United States, United Kingdom, APAC, and India. ECI provides infrastructure, security, operations, and AI solutions within client environments. Through the ELLA platform and technology partnerships, ECI builds and operates practical AI solutions designed for measurable outcomes, secure data handling, and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities

Independently lead AI client engagements from discovery and scoping through production deployment, adoption, documentation, and handover, serving as the accountable engineering lead for the client.
Lead discovery with client leaders, operators, and technical teams to map workflows and identify where AI can save time, reduce risk, or improve quality across investment research, deal flow, trading, portfolio management, risk, valuations, fund operations, investor relations, and compliance.
Own engagement scope and turn business needs into prioritized, buildable use cases with clear success measures based on value, data access, risk, and implementation effort.
Architect, build, and deploy AI agents, integrations, and workflows using TypeScript or Python, ECI platforms, AI coding tools, Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft 365, and appropriate specialist products.
Integrate solutions with client systems, APIs, documents, and data while addressing authentication, permissions, data isolation, audit trails, records retention, retries, and partial failures.
Design evaluations using client examples, verify AI-assisted code and outputs, and apply automated checks and human review before solutions reach production.
Partner with client compliance, security, and IT teams to establish data-handling requirements, approvals, information barriers, and production controls.
Lead client enablement, train users, measure adoption and results against agreed success measures, iterate based on feedback, and document operating procedures and runbooks for handover.
Mentor Associate FDEs and FDEs through technical reviews, client delivery, and professional development; convert recurring client needs into reusable patterns, connectors, and agent skills, and share field insights with ECI product and engineering teams.

Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities)

Five or more years of professional software engineering experience, including experience supporting production systems.
Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM-powered features, agents, or AI-enabled workflows to production users.
Strong programming skills in TypeScript or Python, including development of APIs, integrations, and data workflows.
Experience with retrieval, evaluation, and guardrails for LLM applications, including work across more than one model provider.
Experience integrating third-party systems and APIs and handling authentication, permissions, data access, and failure conditions.
Experience using AI coding agents with the judgment to review, correct, test, and verify generated output.
Ability to understand business processes quickly, communicate technical choices clearly to non-technical stakeholders, and lead client engagements independently and communicate effectively with executive, business, compliance, security, and technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a client-facing engineering role and exposure to hedge funds, private equity, investment banking, asset management, fund administration, or other regulated financial-services environments.
Experience with Azure, Azure AI Foundry, infrastructure as code such as Terraform, and Microsoft 365 technologies including Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Teams, and SharePoint.
Familiarity with investment-industry systems, data, and workflows, including portfolio or order management, fund accounting, research management, market data, private-markets platforms, compliance archiving, reconciliation, or investor reporting.

Working Conditions

Ability to lead client engagements independently while coordinating effectively with distributed ECI product, engineering, industry, security, and account teams.
Ability to work regularly at client sites in the New York area and travel occasionally for business.
Ability to manage multiple client priorities and respond flexibly to deadlines, production issues, and changing engagement needs.
Ability to work beyond normal business hours when necessary to support client delivery, releases, or critical business cycles.
Ability to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other standard office technology for extended periods.
Client onboarding may require background checks, security attestations, personal-trading pre-clearance, holdings reporting, or other controls required by the client.

added.description:
MANTECH
seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Senior AI ML Engineer
. This is currently a hybrid position with two to three days onsite in Ashburn, VA
.

In this role, you will collaborate within a cross-functional team to develop new Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) based solutions into operational pipelines to deliver mission impact for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The ideal candidate will have deep expertise and experience with predictive modeling lifecycles, hands-on experience with machine learning tools and frameworks, and a pragmatic, customer-centric approach to applying ML models to solve complex problems.

Each day CBP oversees the massive flow of people, capital, and products that enter and depart the United States via air, land, sea, and cyberspace. The volume and complexity of both physical and virtual border crossings require the application of solutions to aid officers in detecting threats while promoting efficient trade and travel.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Lead the integration and deployment of trained AI/ML models into production environments (e.g., cloud, edge devices) using MLOps best practices.
Develop and optimize model training & inference pipelines for real-time execution and efficiently handle large-scale data processing.
Work with data science teams to structure automated ML model health monitoring and refresh capabilities.
Implement continuous integration, delivery and training (CI/CD/CT) workflows with commercial and open-source modeling platforms/services.
Coordinate with Data Science and Engineering teams to build scalable feature stores for optimal model training & execution workflows.
Research, evaluate and recommend new tools, applications, software packages for MLOps engineering that can be adopted and approved for use in the CBP environment.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g., Software Engineering, Data Science) to integrate and test multiple candidate AI/ML models and applications for operational assessment.

Minimum Qualifications

HS Diploma/GED and 15-20 years of experience, AS/AA and 13-18 years, BS/BA and 6 years or MS/MA/MBA and 5+ years or PhD/Doctorate and 3+ years.
Hands-on experience with LLMs such as Gemini, Llama, Mistral, or other open-source and commercial models. Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or equivalent custom frameworks. Ability to optimize LLM systems for latency, throughput, scalability, reliability, GPU utilization, and inference cost. Experience deploying machine learning or LLM services in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Demonstrated experience designing and deploying LLM solutions, including the following:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Agentic workflows and tool calling
Prompt engineering and structured outputs
Model fine-tuning, e.g. LoRA
Embedding-based search and semantic retrieval

Strong understanding of transformer architectures, tokenization, embeddings, context windows, inference parameters, and common LLM failure modes. Experience evaluating LLM applications for accuracy, relevance, hallucination, safety, latency, and cost.
Experience with vector databases or search technologies such as OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, Milvus, Qdrant, Pinecone, Weaviate, or pgvector.
Experience designing and integrating RESTful APIs and microservices using frameworks such as FastAPI.
Working knowledge of SQL and experience with relational, document, or NoSQL databases.
Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, logging, and production incident troubleshooting.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, or a related discipline.
Experience training, fine-tuning, quantizing, or serving open-source LLMs using tools such as PyTorch, Ollama, or TensorRT-LLM.
Understanding of AI security risks, including prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool execution, model abuse, and adversarial inputs. Experience building multi-agent systems, multimodal applications, long-context workflows, or human-in-the-loop AI systems.
Knowledge of advanced retrieval techniques, including hybrid search, reranking, query expansion, metadata filtering, and retrieval evaluation.
Experience in LLM projects from initial requirements and proof of concept through production deployment and ongoing optimization.
Strong knowledge of software engineering practices, including version control, code review, automated testing, system design, and technical documentation.

Clearance Requirements

Must be a U.S. Citizen and be able to obtain and maintain a CBP suitability prior to start this position.
The ability to obtain and maintain a Top-Secret clearance.

Physical Requirements

The person in this position needs to occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, or to communicate with co-workers, management, and customers, which may involve delivering presentations,

added.description:
Mechanics Bank is currently searching for an AI Platform Engineer to join our team. Here at Mechanics Bank, we value connection, partnership, long term relationships and working together in person. This role will be working on-site.

The Senior Kubernetes, OpenShift & AI Platform Engineer architects, engineers, secures, automates, and supports the Bank's enterprise Kubernetes and artificial intelligence platform on Red Hat OpenShift, OpenShift Virtualization, and OpenShift AI. The role supports containerized and virtualized workloads, enterprise model serving, large language model inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, agentic AI services, and GPU-enabled workloads. The engineer establishes resilient, observable, governed, and cost-aware platform patterns and partners with Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Application Development, Risk Management, and Service Management to operationalize AI capabilities in a regulated banking environment.

What you will do:

Architect, configure, maintain, patch, upgrade, and optimize production Kubernetes and Red Hat OpenShift clusters.
Administer OpenShift Virtualization and shared platform services, including compute, storage, network, identity, backup, recovery, observability, and certificate dependencies.
Develop reference architectures, engineering standards, runbooks, lifecycle plans, and operational documentation.
Design, configure, and operate AI model-serving and LLM inference workloads using OpenShift AI and approved model-serving runtimes.
Engineer GPU scheduling, quotas, placement, capacity, performance, availability, and cost controls.
Manage model artifacts, serving configurations, deployment, rollback, scaling, monitoring, and retirement.
Design secure RAG architectures using approved data sources, embedding services, vector stores, retrieval controls, reranking, model endpoints, and source traceability.
Support retrieval relevance, grounding, authorization, data freshness, lineage, retention, and quality controls.
Design and support MCP server and agentic AI integration patterns, including authentication, authorization, tool registration, network segmentation, secrets, logging, action traceability, human approval checkpoints, and emergency disablement.
Ensure AI agents and tools operate with least privilege and within approved data and action boundaries.
Build Infrastructure-as-Code, GitOps, CI/CD, MLOps, and operational automation using approved tools.
Create reusable templates, pipelines, operators, validation controls, and self-service capabilities.
Implement platform and AI security controls, vulnerability remediation, audit logging, monitoring, incident response, risk documentation, control testing, and regulatory evidence.
Participate in on-call support, root-cause analysis, problem management, disaster recovery testing, and continuous improvement.
Perform other job duties as assigned by supervisor.

4 Year /Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related discipline preferred. Additional relevant experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
5 years minimum progressive enterprise infrastructure, platform engineering, systems engineering, AI engineering, or closely related technical experience required.
5 years minimum hands-on Kubernetes engineering in production environments required.
3 years minimum Hands-on Red Hat OpenShift engineering and administration required.
2 years minimum Deploying or operating AI/ML, generative AI, or model-serving workloads in containerized environments required.
Experience supporting highly available, mission-critical platforms.
Experience in financial services or another regulated environment is preferred.
Experience integrating platform services with enterprise storage, networking, identity, backup, monitoring, SIEM, CMDB, vulnerability management, and service management solutions.
Red Hat Certified OpenShift Administrator or Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration preferred.
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS) preferred.
Relevant Red Hat OpenShift AI, NVIDIA, cloud AI, machine learning, security, Linux, automation, or infrastructure certification preferred.
Working knowledge of ITIL practices preferred.
Advanced Kubernetes engineering: cluster architecture, control plane operations, scheduling, networking, storage, RBAC, Operators, Helm, autoscaling, policy, and troubleshooting.
Advanced Red Hat OpenShift experience, including OpenShift Container Platform, OpenShift Virtualization, OpenShift AI, OpenShift GitOps, Routes, Operators, Security Context Constraints, and cluster lifecycle management.
AI platform engineering experience with model serving, LLM inference, accelerators/GPUs, KServe or comparable serving frameworks, vLLM or comparable optimized runtimes, model artifacts, inference endpoints, and AI observability.
RAG engineering knowledge, including embeddings, vector stores, retrieval filters, reranking, grounding, source attribution, data entitlements, and evaluation methods.
Understanding of MCP and agentic AI architecture, including server placement, tool integration, identity, authorization, human-in-the-loop controls, auditability, and safe failure handling.
Linux administration, preferably Red Hat Enterprise Linux, and strong knowledge of DNS, TCP/IP, load balancing, storage, virtualization, certificates, and network troubleshooting.
Automation and software engineering using Ansible, Terraform, Git, Python, Bash, PowerShell, APIs, or comparable technologies.
Security and risk knowledge covering identity, secrets, encryption, network policy, image and software supply chain security, vulnerability management, prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agency, backup, recovery, and disaster recovery.
Ability to communicate complex platform and AI concepts to engineers, application owners, cybersecurity, risk partners, auditors, and leadership.
Ability to mentor peers, lead technical decisions, document standards, and manage complex work independently.
